newsitem.title: INDIA: Kashmir's ruling party disputes blast deaths claim.
newsitem.headline: Kashmir's ruling party disputes blast deaths claim.

text.p: Kashmir's new ruling party, the National Conference, denied on Monday that Moslem separatist guerrillas attacked a party worker's house and said a blast which killed at least five people was part of an army attack on militants hiding there.
Accounts of the incident from the party, the army and local news agenies contradicted each other on many points.
"They are trying to put blame on the army," an army spokesman told Reuters in the state capital of Srinagar. "We strongly deny their allegations that army has blasted the house."

The explosion was at the Anantnag district home of Abdul Rashid Nadaf, a worker for the anti-separatist National Conference which won last month's election in Moslem-majority Jammu and Kashmir state and has installed its leader, Farooq Abdullah, as chief minister.
A police spokesman said there were two blasts which were still being investigated.

The Press Trust of India and the United News of India, quoting official sources, reported a single blast and said seven relatives of the politician were killed in an attack by suspected separatist rebels.
National Conference general secretary Sheikh Nazir, a brother of the new chief minister, said the five dead were separatist guerrillas who were hiding at the house, not attacking it.

"The people were killed in an anti-militancy operation," Nazir told Reuters. "Our party worker was not the target of the blast. Some militants of Muslim Mujahideen were hiding in the house and security forces blasted the house."
